text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers.

- The Cypriot court said it could not rule in the case of Slovenia against the Yugoslav bank Beogradska Banka, saying the matter of assets of the former Yugoslavia should be solved through negotiations.
- Slovenia so far has not restricted official relations with Bosnia over its failure to agree on the distribution of ambassadorial posts according to political groups.
- The Slovenian Minister of Labour Anton Rop said the pension system reform will be presented to parliament in autumn.
- The government on Tuesday sent to parliament the 1997 budget proposal, which was adopted last week.

- Michael Jackson's Ljubljana concert, which was scheduled for Friday, has been postponed till September 9 because less than 20,000 tickets have been sold, while organisers expected some 70,000 visitors.
- The chemical firm Fenolit started searching for barrels of chemical waste, which are believed to have been buried in the ground near the factory two decades ago.
- The wheat harvest is good this year despite much hail, which damaged many wheat fields in Slovenia,
- Slovenia's Red Cross on Tuesday sent 60 tons of food and medicine to Albania in order to help the poor.
- The government expects to name the management board of the Slovenian Development Company by August 15.
- There are rumours that two new daily newpapers might be launched in the autumn. Currently the country with two million people has four dailies.
